title: Shadda: say the letter twice

bigIdea.text: A small 'w'-shaped sign on a letter means the letter is doubled: you say it once to close the syllable before it, and once more with its vowel, in one smooth go.

proper.text: Shadda ( ّ ) means the letter counts twice: the first copy has sukun and closes the syllable before it; the second carries the vowel written with the shadda. In the middle of a word, ـبَّـ is read بْ + بَ ('b-ba').
Hold the doubled letter a moment longer than a single one, but put no gap and no vowel between the two copies.
The vowel goes with the shadda: a fatha or damma sits above it. A kasra belongs below the letter, but many mushaf prints draw it just under the shadda instead. It is still a kasra: read 'i'.
A letter with shadda is called mushaddad. ن and م with shadda also get a nasal hum (ghunnah) of about two counts; Stage 2 teaches it.

visual.caption: Shadda alone, then with fatha, damma and kasra.

memoryHook.text: Shadda = the same letter twice: once to close, once to go.

extras.text: English does something similar across words: in 'midday' one d closes 'mid' and the next opens 'day'. A shadda does that inside one word.
Persian/Urdu readers know the tashdid sign. In recitation make the doubling clearly audible every time; it can change the meaning of a word.

note.text: The last ب has a shadda with a kasra: close on ب, then say it again with 'i'.
ي doubled, with a fatha, then a long alif.
ن doubled: you also hear a nasal hum (ghunnah).

drills.prompt: Single, then doubled: بَتَ then بَتَّ. Hold the doubled ت a moment; no gap, no extra vowel.
Doubled with each vowel: بَتَّ بَتُّ بَتِّ (batta, battu, batti).

tip.text: تَ is one 'ta'. تَّ is ت doubled: close on 't' after the vowel before it, then say 'ta'.

questions.q: What does a shadda tell you?
options: The letter is doubled: once with sukun, once with its vowel
Stretch the vowel for two counts
explain: Right.
A shadda letter is said twice, not skipped.
Stretching is a long vowel (madd).
Stopping is shown by pause signs.

questions.q: In the middle of a word, how is بَّ read?
explain: Right.
Loudness is not doubling; you need two copies.
There is no alif, so no long vowel.
The fatha on the shadda must be read.

questions.q: What is a letter with shadda called?
explain: Right.
Sakin is a letter with sukun.
Munawwan words end in tanween (lesson 21).
A stretched vowel is a madd (lesson 22).

questions.q: In many mushaf prints, where can the kasra of a doubled letter be drawn?
options: Just under the shadda, above the letter
At the end of the word
explain: Right; read it as 'i' as usual.
Each mark belongs to its own letter.
The vowel is always written.
Marks sit on their letter, not at the word's end.

questions.q: Which letters with shadda also get a nasal hum (ghunnah)?
explain: Right: about two counts of humming through the nose (Stage 2).
ب and ت are not nasal letters.
ر and ل have no ghunnah of their own.
ق and ك are not nasal letters.

questions.q: What is the most common mistake with shadda?
options: Saying the letter only once, too quickly
Joining it to the vowel before it
explain: Right: a missed shadda can change the word.
A slightly longer hold is correct.
The first copy should join the vowel before it.
The vowel on the shadda must be read.

questions.q: Which sign means 'this letter is doubled'?
explain: Right.
Sukun means no vowel.
Tanween adds '-un'.
Kasra is the vowel 'i'.

questions.q: The shadda on a letter carries a damma. How do you finish the doubled letter?
explain: Right: the second copy takes the vowel written with the shadda.
That would need a fatha.
That would need a kasra.
The second copy always has the written vowel.

questions.q: How long is a doubled letter compared with a single one?
options: A little longer, as one smooth doubled sound
Twice as long, with a pause in between
explain: Right.
Then the doubling is lost.
There is no pause or vowel between the two copies.
Counts measure vowels and ghunnah, not a doubled letter.

questions.q: In ـتَّـ, the first copy of ت belongs to…
options: The syllable before it (it closes it)
explain: Right.
A shadda works inside the word.
Both copies are heard.
The second copy carries the vowel; the first closes the syllable before.

questions.q: Which English word has a doubled sound like a shadda?
explain: Right: one d closes, the next opens.
Only one d.
Only one d.
Only one d.

questions.q: You see نّ with a fatha. What does the rule ask you to add there?
options: A nasal hum (ghunnah) of about two counts
explain: Right.
Qalqalah is a bounce on ق ط ب ج د with sukun.
No pause is marked there.
There is no alif, so no long vowel.

questions.q: Which pair shows a single letter versus a doubled one?
explain: Right: the second has a shadda.
تْ has a sukun, not a shadda.
تً has tanween, not a shadda.
تِ only changes the vowel.

remnote: Shadda ( ّ ) == The letter is doubled: first copy with sukun, second with the vowel
Kasra on a doubled letter in many prints == Drawn just under the shadda, above the letter
ن or م with shadda == Doubled, plus a nasal hum (ghunnah) of about 2 counts
taskNow: Say بَتَ then بَتَّ five times, making the doubled ت clearly longer, record the fifth time, then press Play mine (step 5, Practise) and compare it with the reference.
